behavior: Allocation-event call windows record initial/final/peak scoped payload plus tracking headers. Lifetime high-water is not used as an individual call peak. Call/owner IDs and last font/raster reports are exposed.

Budget reservations and scope deltas share a synchronization boundary. Simultaneous host/process admission includes every active call; existing pre-call reservations remain a floor and cannot be lent to concurrent admissions. Admission occupancy is distinct from the call's actual owned-byte counters.

Call completion atomically transfers old cache/temporary reservations to retained ownership. Raster pixels retain their own permits until copied/dropped; cache retirement leaves existing pixels and shapes valid.
Output destruction is synchronized with the owning call window, so another thread cannot invalidate the fixed returned-output exclusion while private construction is running.

An overrun releases rejected derived output and remains distinguishable from a missing glyph. Generic atlas retry does not swallow it. Required source and pending state remain available for a later attempt. With no headroom and existing pending uploads, yield before starting the next opaque call.
